reauth_cloud_control.title: Sign in to Shelly again for cloud control
reauth_cloud_control.description:
Shelly Cloud rejected the stored sign-in that the cloud control channel uses. Sign in with your Shelly account to restore control of your virtual components.

Your Authorization cloud key is a different credential and is unaffected — polling has kept running the whole time. The password is used once to sign in and is never stored.

data_description.password: Used once to sign in and then discarded. Only the resulting token is stored.

init.title: Shelly Cloud DIY options
init.description: Adjust how often the integration polls Shelly Cloud for state, when a silent device counts as offline and, optionally, the local gateway URL used by the historical-data service. Device selection follows on the next step.

data.offline_after_minutes: Report a device as offline after (minutes)
data.relay_fault_detection: Warn about a relay that no longer opens
data.local_gateway_url: Local gateway URL (optional, for EM historical data)
data.device_health_detection: Warn about devices in poor health
data.device_health_firmware: Count a pending firmware update as a finding
data.cloud_control: Control virtual components over the cloud (unsupported)

data_description.poll_interval: 3–60 s. Lower values feel snappier but consume more of Shelly's 1 req/s rate-limit budget.
data_description.offline_after_minutes: 2–1440 min, default 30. Each device's "Reporting" sensor turns off once the device has been silent this long. It is only a base value: a device that is naturally quieter earns a wider window on its own, and battery or BLE devices are handled separately. Lowering it therefore mainly speeds up detection on devices that report continuously, such as power-metering plugs.
data_description.relay_fault_detection: On by default. Watches every switching channel that meters its own output and warns when the relay reports itself as open while a real load is still flowing through it — a contact that has welded shut. Turn this off if a Shelly of yours sits in a two-way circuit, where the other switch can push current through the meter while the relay is genuinely open.
data_description.local_gateway_url: Only needed if you use a local Shelly gateway to back-fill historical energy data.
data_description.device_health_detection: On by default. Interprets data every poll already returns: Wi-Fi signal (warning at -70 dBm, error at -85 dBm), component temperature (70 °C / 85 °C), free memory and free storage (under 20 % / 10 %), a restart the device is still waiting for, and any component reporting its own error. It costs no extra requests. Bluetooth (BLU) devices are judged only on the signal their gateway reports for them, and Gen1 devices are not judged at all. Only a component's own temperature counts, never an external Add-on probe.
data_description.device_health_firmware: Off by default. Adds "a firmware update is available" as a finding. On a typical account most devices have one pending, so switching this on tends to keep the card permanently lit — which is exactly what stops you noticing the findings that matter.
data_description.cloud_control:
Off by default, and worth reading before switching on. Virtual components (an irrigation controller's zones, a script's switch) can be read over the documented Shelly Cloud API but not written — every documented route answers "no such route". Switching them is possible only over an **undocumented** channel, which Shelly support declared unsupported on 2026-07-27 and can change or withdraw without notice.

What it costs: your Shelly account sign-in (asked for on the next step; the password is used once and never stored) and a second connection to Shelly Cloud.

What it gives you: a switch for each virtual boolean, but **only on devices your account owns**. A shared device is refused by Shelly itself, and no switch appears for it. The switch is created **in addition** to the existing read-only sensor of the same component, never instead of it, so nothing you have already built on that sensor breaks.

Switching this off again deletes the stored sign-in.

cloud_control.title: Sign in to Shelly for cloud control
cloud_control.description:
Cloud control needs your Shelly account sign-in, because the channel it uses accepts an account token rather than the Authorization cloud key.

The password is used once to sign in and is **never stored** — only the resulting token is, and switching the option off again deletes it. Nothing is saved unless this sign-in succeeds.

download_and_convert_history.name: Download and convert historical energy data
download_and_convert_history.description: Fetches CSV exports from the local Shelly gateway and imports them into Home Assistant's long-term statistics.

gateway_url.name: Gateway URL
gateway_url.description: Base URL of the local gateway (overrides the one configured in options).

device_id.name: Device ID
device_id.description: Optional — restrict the import to a single EM device. All EM devices are imported if omitted.

replace_device.name: Replace device
replace_device.description: Transplant a dead Shelly's Home Assistant identity (entity IDs, the HA device, name, area, history and every automation/dashboard reference) onto a new Shelly of the same model, so you don't have to reconfigure Home Assistant after a hardware swap. Enable the new device first.

old_device.name: Old (replaced) device
old_device.description: The Shelly device that broke or was removed.

new_device.name: New device
new_device.description: The new Shelly that should take over. Enable it first.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only show what would change, without applying it.

force.name: Force (ignore model mismatch)
force.description: Proceed even if the two devices report different models. Only use this if the channel layout matches.

fleet_map.name: Fleet map
fleet_map.description: Read-only overlay: matches every cloud device to its local (native Shelly) twin by MAC, suggests names, and flags any device whose control runs over the cloud. Writes a report to your notifications. Safe to run anytime — it changes nothing unless you explicitly opt in.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only show the report, without applying any native name suggestions. On by default.

apply_native_name_suggestions.name: Apply native name suggestions
apply_native_name_suggestions.description: Also copy each cloud alias onto its matched local (native Shelly) device. Only writes the technical name, never a name you set yourself. Requires turning Dry run off. Off by default.

rate_limited.title: Shelly Cloud is rate-limiting this integration
rate_limited.description:
Shelly Cloud allows about one request per second, and it has been rejecting this integration's requests ({entry_title}) for the last couple of minutes.

**This is not a problem with your Authorization cloud key.** Shelly signals the rate limit as an HTTP 401 response whose body contains `max_req` — the same status code a rejected key would produce, but a different cause. Nothing needs to be re-entered.

What to do:

1. Check whether something else is polling Shelly Cloud with the same key at the same time — the Shelly mobile app, a second Home Assistant entry for the same account, or your own scripts.
2. Raise the poll interval in the integration options (Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure). The default of 5 seconds leaves room, but the integration also makes occasional extra lookups on top of each poll.

Entities become available again on the first poll that gets through, and this message disappears on its own.

missing_devices.title: Selected devices are missing from your Shelly account
missing_devices.description:
You selected {count} device(s) for {entry_title} that Shelly Cloud has not reported for the last 24 hours, so no entities are created for them.

Device(s): {device_ids}

The most likely causes are that the device was removed from your Shelly account, or — for a Shelly BLU device — that the Bluetooth gateway bridging it has been offline for a long time.

What to do:

1. If this is a Shelly BLU device, check that the mains-powered Shelly that bridges it is online.
2. Otherwise, check whether the device still appears in the Shelly app under the same account.
3. If it is gone for good, open Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure, click through to the device list and save. The missing device is no longer offered there, so it drops out of your selection automatically. Then run the **Find Shelly devices no longer in your account** action (Developer tools → Actions, leave Dry run on) to see which Home Assistant devices are left over.

This message clears by itself as soon as the device reports again, or after you save your device selection again.

history_import_failed.title: Historical energy data could not be imported
history_import_failed.description:
The historical-data sync for {entry_title} has run twice without importing anything. Live device data is unaffected — only the import of past energy readings into long-term statistics.

Most often the local gateway URL is wrong, or the gateway is not reachable from Home Assistant.

What to do:

1. Open Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure and check the local gateway URL, including the scheme and port (for example `http://192.168.1.50:8080`).
2. Confirm the gateway is running and reachable from Home Assistant.
3. If you no longer use it, clear the field to switch the import off.

The sync runs once at startup and then daily. To check a correction right away, run the **Download and convert historical energy data** action from Developer tools → Actions instead of waiting.

relay_fault.title: A Shelly relay is no longer switching off
relay_fault.description:
{count} switching channel(s) on {entry_title} reported the relay as **open** while the device's own power meter reported a load still flowing through it, for at least two minutes.

Device(s): {devices}

This is what a welded relay contact looks like. The actuator still accepts commands and still reports *off*, but the load never actually switches off — so anything that relies on switching it off (an automation, a schedule, a motion sensor) silently stops working, and the load keeps consuming power.

What to do:

1. Check whether the load really is still running. The "Relay fault" diagnostic sensor on the device carries the measured wattage as an attribute.
2. If it is, treat the actuator as defective and plan to replace it. A contact that welds once tends to do it again, and it cannot be switched off in software — only at the breaker.
3. If the load is genuinely not running, the wiring may be feeding current past this relay (for example a two-way circuit). You can switch this warning off in the integration options.

The warning clears on its own once the channel has agreed with its own meter again for five minutes.

device_health.title: Some Shelly devices are reporting problems
device_health.description:
{count} device(s) on {entry_title} crossed a health threshold and stayed across it for at least five minutes.

Findings: {summary}

Device(s): {devices}

Everything behind this comes from the status data the integration already polls — nothing extra was requested from Shelly Cloud. What the individual findings mean:

- **Wi-Fi signal** — the device sits at -70 dBm or worse. The link still works, but it retransmits a lot and the device will drop off the cloud more often than the rest of your fleet. Move the device, move the access point, or add one closer.
- **Temperature** — a component reports 70 °C or more. Usually a device packed into an insulated wall box, or one switching more current than its installation allows for. Only a component's own temperature is judged; an external probe on a Shelly Add-on is not, because a sensor in a boiler pipe is hot by design.
- **Free memory / Free storage** — under 20 % is left. Scripts, schedules and over-the-air updates need that room; below 10 % the firmware starts refusing work and rebooting.
- **Restart pending** — a configuration change has not been applied yet. Restart the device from the Shelly app.
- **Component error** — the device itself is reporting this one, most often a wired add-on sensor that no longer answers.
- **Firmware update** — information only, and off by default. It appears here only if you switched it on in the options.

This is one card for the whole account, never one per device. It clears by itself as soon as every device is back below its thresholds, and the whole check can be switched off under Settings → Devices & services → Shelly Cloud DIY → Configure.
